text:
karen: Heads-up — frost-int8 canary is producing NDJSON parse errors for streaming funcalls. Not truncated JSON, but extra line-breaks inserted mid-object making NDJSON invalid.

micah: Extra newlines? Like "\n" characters appearing in the middle of a JSON object? That's odd. Any sample?

karen: Yep. FP16 mirror is clean (~0.2% NDJSON fail). frost-int8 at ~1.4% on 3k streaming samples. Example (stream chunk boundary trimmed):```...{"tool":"append","args":{"text":"line1\nline2\npartial"}
...```
Notice a raw linebreak landed between chunks causing the NDJSON line to split and fail the line-reader.

sasha: Could be a streaming chunk reassembly + tokenization change. If the model emits actual "\\n" characters (two-char escape) vs literal newline differs by token composition after quantization. Run a streaming vs non-streaming replay.

diego: Also check for CRLF vs LF differences in the runtime streaming buffer; quant fast-path might flush micro-chunks differently.

karen: Repro command I used:```for i in $(seq 1 3000); do curl -s -N -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/invoke -d '{"model":"frost-int8","prompt":"<ndjson-stream-test>","max_tokens":200,"stream":true}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" | tee -a out.stream; done; jq -R 'select(test("\\n$"))' out.stream | wc -l``` Yields the NDJSON line-splitting count.

ci-bot: Canary frost-int8 rolled to 25% at 3880012000 - https://deploys.redwood/3880012000 (alert threshold: 0.5% ndjson-split)

micah: Quick mitigation ideas: 1) on proxy, buffer NDJSON streaming lines and attempt reassembly for common single-newline splits (soft repair), 2) spin a no-stream mirror and disable CB for canary pool, 3) add a tokenization diff test between fp16 vs int8 for escape sequences and explicit newline tokens.

sasha: If reassembly brings visible failures <0.3% we can keep canary at low traffic while infra/ML digests. Also add an onboard stress test that simulates streaming chunk boundaries and checks NDJSON integrity.

diego: For root cause, run a controlled micro-batch where we force emissions to cross the chunk size boundary and capture token ids emitted across the split for fp16 vs int8. If the int8 model emits a literal newline token where fp16 emits escaped "\\n", that explains it.

karen: Will run the micro-batch token-id capture and produce a diff. For immediate impact I've reduced canary to 5% and enabled fp16 mirror. Also adding the proxy reassembly heuristic for canary routes.

deploy-bot: Canary frost-int8 scaled back to 5% at 3880012300 (actioned by @sasha).

micah: Nice. When you post the token-id diff link, I'll start the quant-bisect to see which packing/merge step introduced newline/escape shifts. If it's runtime chunking, we may need a small patch to the streaming flusher.

karen: Update (20m): no-CB + non-stream mirror dropped NDJSON-splits to 0.28% on a 2k sample replay. Proxy reassembly reduces customer-facing failures to 0.07%. Attaching logs in the incident doc.

sasha: Good signal. Action items: 1) keep canary at 5% with fp16 mirror, 2) keep proxy reassembly soft-fix, 3) add streaming-chunk-boundary test to int8 onboard suite, 4) micah to run quant-bisect on newline/escape tokenization behavior, 5) diego to sanity-check streaming flusher timing in int8 fast-path.

karen: Filing incident note now with micro-batch captures and sample clips. Thanks all. :pray:
